summary.plain: The JUNO collaboration's first report on how well the detector itself works: how much light it collects, how sharply it measures energy, and how clear its liquid is.
summary.technical: First reported in-situ performance figures for the JUNO central detector: light yield 1,785 photoelectrons/MeV, energy resolution 3.4% at 0.511 MeV γ-rays, and liquid-scintillator attenuation length 20.6 m at 430 nm.

title: Initial performance results of the JUNO detector

why_it_matters.note: CORRECTED 2026-09-18: the prior quote ('attenuation length of 20.6 m at 430 nm, exceeding expectations') could not be verified verbatim against any fetched source (the cited page, cpc.ihep.ac.cn, renders as a JS shell with no article text reachable by a plain fetch). Replaced with a verbatim sentence from the paper's own full text (arXiv:2511.14590) that supports the same claim.
why_it_matters.quote: The measured attenuation lengths are 20.6 m for the LS at 430 nm and greater than 70.0 m for water at 400 nm, outperforming the simulated values of 20.0 m and 40.0 m, respectively.
why_it_matters.value: Confirms the detector meets or exceeds its design specifications ahead of its long-term physics program.
